rules.title: Every word with kanji has a kana reading
rules.why: Furigana and the kana-only answers come from it; without one a beginner can't read the word.

rules.title: Every item has a JLPT level
rules.why: Levels decide what a beginner meets first and how the exam prints its kanji.

rules.title: Every item has a meaning
rules.why: Recognition cards ask for it.

rules.title: Every word has a topic from the taxonomy
rules.why: Words by topic must cover every word.

rules.title: No word appears twice with the same spelling and reading
rules.why: Duplicates split a learner's progress and show twice in a session.

rules.title: Furigana are kana
rules.why: Ruby over kanji must be readable by a beginner.

rules.title: Furigana markup spells the same sentence
rules.why: If the ruby version drifts from the text, the learner sees a different sentence than the one checked.

rules.title: Furigana on a whole word match its dictionary reading
rules.why: Generated furigana can misread a compound (目撃者 もくげきもの); the word list says how it's read.

rules.title: A kanji's key reading is one of its on or kun readings
rules.why: The key reading is shown over the kanji on its card.

rules.title: Every kanji has example words
rules.why: Readings are learned and quizzed through words, as the JLPT tests them.

rules.title: A kanji's quiz word contains it and its wrong options differ from the answer
rules.why: The reading quiz asks how that word is read.

rules.title: Kanji quiz words with fewer than 3 exam-style wrong options
rules.why: These are topped up from other words' readings, which is easier than the real exam.

rules.title: Every question has a valid answer and distinct options
rules.why: A wrong key or two identical options makes a question unanswerable.

rules.title: Options per question match the JLPT: 4, or 3 for 即時応答 and 発話表現
rules.why: The exam's format is part of what's being practised.

rules.title: 漢字読み questions underline a word with kanji
rules.why: The part tests reading the underlined kanji word.

rules.title: Questions and lessons point at items and texts that exist
rules.why: A broken link drops a question's text or the words its mistakes should send to review.

rules.title: Full-length mocks have the official number of questions in every part
rules.why: They stand in for the real exam.

rules.title: Reading passages are close to the official length
rules.why: Passage length is a large part of what makes each level's reading hard.

rules.title: Graded reading texts are within the level's official passage lengths
rules.why: A practice text much shorter or longer than any passage on that level's paper trains the wrong reading stamina.

rules.title: Example and lesson sentences suit their level's length
rules.why: Beginners read short sentences first: up to 30 characters at N5, 40 at N4, 55 at N3, 70 at N2.

rules.title: Every grammar point has at least two example sentences
rules.why: One example isn't enough to see how a pattern bends to different words.

rules.title: A lesson's grammar point isn't above the lesson's level
rules.why: Beginners shouldn't meet a harder level's grammar as the point of a lesson.

rules.title: Newcomer phrases and scenes use polite form only
rules.why: The learner copies what they hear; every sentence should be safe to say to anyone (です/ます, or a polite set phrase).

rules.title: Newcomer lines suit their stage or level
rules.why: Early stages are short chunks a beginner can say in one breath: 16 characters up to stage 3, then 35; scenes 14, 20, 28 and 35 by level.

rules.title: Listening scenes have a valid gist question
rules.why: Three options with the answer among them, or the learner can't get it right.
